content.text: San Tin Technopole (including the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park in the Loop)

Located at the heart of the Northern Metropolis and in close proximity to Shenzhen's innovation and technology (I&T) zone in Huangang and Futian, San Tin Technopole will become a hub for clustered I&T development that creates synergy with Shenzhen I&T Zone. Besides, it will contribute to the development of the South-North dual engine (finance - I&T) for Hong Kong, and become a new community for quality, healthy and green living.

Together with the the Hong Kong-Shenzhen Innovation and Technology Park (HSITP) in the Loop, San Tin Technopole has a total development area of over 600 ha, half (300 ha) of it will be I&T land. The I&T land are capable of accommodating about 7 million square metres of gross floor area, equivalent to 17 Science Parks, and comparable to the size of the 300 ha I&T zone in Shenzhen on the other side of the Shenzhen River.
This showcases the determination of the Government to promote I&T, as well as to develop the Northern Metropolis into a "new international I&T city".

The construction of the first three buildings in Phase 1 of the HSITP has been completed. Tenants from life and health technology, microelectronics, new energy, AI and other pillar industries are gradually moving in. The construction of the other five buildings will be completed progressively from 2027. HSITP has also rolled out parcels of the remaining land in Phase 1 to invite expression of interest from the market.

This year, HSITP will complete Phase 2 planning for the development scale and distribution of industries to finalise HSITP's overall layout and consider offering work spaces flexibly to companies under the "moving in while construction is underway" approach.

For the area outside the HSITP in the Loop, the Planning Department and the Civil Engineering and Development Department jointly commissioned a study in October 2021 to formulate a Recommended Outline Development Plan proposing land uses. The statutory planning process completed in September 2024.

Site formation and engineering infrastructure works for development of the San Tin Technopole Phase 1 Stage 1 commenced in December 2024. We target to deliver about 20 hectares of new I&T sites in phases, beginning in 2026-27, for the HKSTP Corporation's development and operation.

The I&T Park will be served by two major cross-boundary rail links, namely the proposed Northern Link (NOL) Spur Line passing through San Tin Technopole and the HSITP at the Loop connecting to the new Huanggang Port, and the existing Lok Ma Chau Spur Line with Lok Ma Chau Station.
For details, please refer to the study's website:
https://nm-santintech.hk/en/

content.text: I&T Park (located mostly to the north of San Tin Highway/Fanling Highway)

Together with the HSITP at the Loop, San Tin Technopole has a total development area of over 600 ha, half (300 ha) of it will be I&T land. The I&T land are capable of accommodating about 7 million square metres of gross floor area, equivalent to 17 Science Parks, and comparable to the size of the 300 ha I&T zone in Shenzhen on the other side of the Shenzhen River.
This showcases the determination of the Government to promote I&T, as well as to develop the Northern Metropolis into a “new international I&T city”.

We have designed connected land parcels of different sizes, including some sizable ones, to provide flexibility so as to cater for I&T facilities of different scales. We have provided maximum flexibility under the land use zones for I&T land.

Site formation for the first batch of I&T land commence in end 2024. The target is to deliver about 20 hectares of new I&T sites in phases, beginning in 2026‑27, for the Hong Kong Science and Technology Parks Corporation’s development and operation.

The I&T Park will be served by two major cross-boundary rail links, namely the proposed Northern Link (NOL) Spur Line passing through San Tin Technopole and the HSITP at the Loop connecting to the new Huanggang Port, and the existing Lok Ma Chau Spur Line with Lok Ma Chau Station.
San Tin Town Centre (located to the south of San Tin Highway/Fanling Highway)
Will supply about 50 000 public and private housing units, mostly within 500m walking distance from the San Tin Station.

The area is planned as a self-sufficient, integrated neighbourhood with comprehensive public and community facilities including an iconic recreational and cultural complex, government, institution and community facilities. It can also provide support for the needs of the I&T Park.

Built around the proposed San Tin Station of the NOL Main Line, San Tin Town Centre is the intersection of the NOL Main Line and Spur Line. There are four major roads connecting with the surrounding areas (viz. San Tin Highway, Fanling Highway, San Sham Road and the proposed Northern Metropolis Highway).

subzones.title: Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area

content.text: Ngau Tam Mei (NTM) is situated to the east of Fairview Park in Yuen Long and south of the future San Tin Technopole. NTM and San Tin are intermediate stations along the future Northern Link (NOL) Main Line, just one station apart. There is potential for NTM to create synergy effect with the innovation and technology (I&T) industry in San Tin Technopole.

The 2024 Policy Address announced that over 80 hectares (ha) of land has been reserved in the Northern Metropolis for the Northern Metropolis University Town (NMUT), where local post‑secondary institutions will be encouraged to introduce more branded programmes, research collaboration and exchange projects with renowned Mainland and overseas institutions in a flexible and innovative manner. In particular, land has been reserved in the NTM New Development Area (hereinafter referred to as “NTM”) for developing the NMUT, the third medical school and an integrated medical teaching and research hospital (integrated hospital).

About 46 ha of land has been reserved in NTM for developing UniTown@NTM, which will facilitate the I&T development of surrounding areas such as San Tin Technopole, to provide talent support at “research, academic and industry” front, promote integrated development of education, technology and talents, and promote Hong Kong as an international hub for high-calibre talents.

About 9 ha of land has also been reserved in NTM for developing a new integrated hospital providing about 3,000 beds. The integrated hospital will provide comprehensive healthcare services for the existing and new population in the Northern Metropolis. The integrated hospital will also provide teaching, training and research facilities to complement the development of the life and health technology industry in San Tin Technopole and Hong Kong at large.

To capitalise on the development opportunities brought about by the NTM Station on the NOL Main Line and serve the future workers and students at NTM, a comprehensive residential community is planned around the station in the western part of the study area, with a view to developing a “15-minute neighbourhood”.
For detailed information on NTM, please refer to the following website:
https://nm-ntm.hk/
Artist's Impression for Illustrative Purpose Only

We have previously conducted a feasibility study on the brownfield sites at Sha Po to the east of the future Northern Link (NOL) Au Tau Station.  In 2023, about 16 hectares of land therein was rezoned for public housing and community facilities uses.  Considering that the NOL is scheduled to be commissioned in 2034, which will bring further development potential to the area, and that this area can provide residential and community support to the nearby innovation and technology enterprises in San Tin Technopole and post-secondary institutions in Ngau Tam Mei, there is scope to consider expanding the development area around Sha Po (initially estimated to increase to about 30 hectares).  The development will be taken forward in the form of a NDA, with a higher proportion of private housing, supported by appropriate community facilities.

The Development Bureau has commissioned the MTR Corporation Limited to conduct a land use review study for about 30 hectares of land in the vicinity of Au Tau Station.  The study results will be announced within 2026.
